institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Get a new experience

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I liked the thought about being able to communicate with the Norwegians, and in that way become more included in the social life of the study and in general in the city. Beside that, the nature was a plus and it was easy to get to from the city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine and if you couldn't find any answers, there exchange mail had relative fast response time

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not that much, invitation to the first intro week and then a lot of different arrangements

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: When you are from Scandinavia and go on exchange in the fall, you cannot get anything through the university and it can be hard to find something that isn't really expensive, targeting exchange students thats doesn't have a better option. Beside that, and all the money used on rent, it is nice living only with exchange students. I will recommend checking out the links on the university webside a bit before if you want a cheaper place to live

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive but it wasn't that much different from the others. The student living in student housing often life closer to each other, so there is a bit more transportation time, but in the summer it is not a problem

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember that much. I had a bit difficulties with the learning agreement but nothing that couldn't get fixed, I just took some time

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Before arrival you could email the exchange office about a lot of things or after arriving there where a physical place you could get IT help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, but one of them we were only 3 exchange student from Copenhagen, so it ended up being almost selfstudie. It was a really nice course, but maybe have that in mind with small more niche courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have a problem, you can always send an email and wait for there answers, they are often usable

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that the courses where easier level through the semester, but their exams wary a lot from what we are used to, but not in a negative way

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost only lectures, no exercise classes, or else without a teacher. So it is a bit more selfstudy / exam reading

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunologi, Obesity, Introduction to molecular medicine, Molecular medical bacteriology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all, but maybe it would be nice to have either Immunology or Introduction to molecular medicine on 15 ECTS, so you have one exam less

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The price of alcohol

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruit and vegestables were expensive, and the sortiment of veggie and lactose free stuff was really small

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of possibilities, both sports through the university NTNUi and fitness. I was also possible to be a part of the studies introweek for the masters students or be a volunteer at samfundet, the big student house for all students in trondheim.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If it is possible, try to be a part of UKA, it is Norways biggest cultural festival, that is in trondheim every second year

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to other parts of Norway, maybe even Sweden or Findland. Go on small cabin trips, which you can rent through the university for 50NOK pr night.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy, a lot like Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take all the opportunities you get and meet a lot of new people. You dont have to be friends with everyone, but it is easy to connect with people there

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it was familiar

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun, enjoy the nature and get some good friends, also at you study

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and the experiences I got. Volunteering at UKA, meeting a lot internationals but also Norwegians. A lot of weekends trip, to see different parts of Norway.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Find enough time for all the things you want to do

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
